event.what_happened: The US-Iran conflict that began on 2026-02-28 cut shipments through the Strait of Hormuz and drove oil sharply higher. Brent averaged $124 in October and fell below $100 in early November as flows through the strait recovered. Attacks continue: Reuters reported three vessels struck in the strait on 2026-11-23.
event.how_it_reaches_markets: Oil prices feed inflation and therefore rate expectations; shipping disruption; risk-off moves on escalation.

sourced_facts.text: EIA, 2026-03-10: Brent 'has risen sharply following the onset of military action in the Middle East' and 'settled at $94 per barrel on March 9'; shipments through the Strait of Hormuz had fallen

Brent spot averaged $124 a barrel in October 2026 and fell below $100 on 2026-11-04; EIA forecasts about $100 for November and December (Short-Term Energy Outlook, November 2026 edition, released 2026-11-10)

EIA estimates Middle East production shut-ins at 2.5 million barrels a day in October, down from 10.9 million at the peak in May, and expects exports from Iran to remain constrained through the forecast period
Same outlook: 'the U.S.-Iran conflict began on February 28'; attacks on oil tankers continued, and flows through the strait continued 'using ship-to-ship transfers along Oman's coast'
EIA, 2026-11-19: oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz rose in the third quarter and stayed near that level in October; by 2026-11-18 Brent had fallen more than $30 from its October average

unconfirmed_facts: Reuters, 2026-11-24: three vessels were struck by unidentified projectiles on 2026-11-23 while sailing east through the Strait of Hormuz, citing the UK Maritime Trade Operations office; all crew accounted for. Read as carried by The Jerusalem Post and The Times of Israel, not at Reuters or at the UK office
2026-11-24: Brent settled more than 2% higher; opened at 90.97 in Asia on 2026-11-25: attributed to Reuters in a repost; original not read
A US-Iran memorandum of understanding signed in June 2026 and a US naval blockade of Iranian ports: reported by ABC News; no government document read

notes: 'Both governments' means the United States and Iran. Brent is read from the daily spot series published by the EIA (FRED: DCOILBRENTEU). An attack counts when reported by Reuters or AP, or listed by the UK Maritime Trade Operations office.

Added 2026-11-28: the first condition counts a ceasefire or agreement announced on or after 2026-11-26, the day the conditions were written. A memorandum reported for June 2026 did not stop the attacks and is not counted.

counter_view.text: Supply is coming back: production shut in has fallen from 10.9 to 2.5 million barrels a day and Brent from an October average of $124 to under $100. The $80 line is our own choice. If the economy has adjusted to oil near $100, the risk could fade well before our conditions say so.
